title: Reactionary Feminists Offer Bad Solutions to Real Problems
summary: Reactionary feminist writers Mary Harrington and Louise Perry dress up arguments for marriage and sexual restraint in Marxist rhetoric. But they also point to the limits of liberal feminism — limits that the Left needs to grapple with.
reason: The piece gestures at the representational vs. structural distinction in feminist politics but stays at the level of ideological critique rather than illuminating a capture mechanism or routing architecture in operation.

title: The Dollar’s Power Never Came From Oil
summary: The emergence of the dollar as the world’s currency was the result of the rise of the US as the preeminent global power. But the slow erosion of US economic and political power will not automatically spell the end of the dollar system.
reason: This is primarily a representational-level debate about currency hegemony narratives rather than illuminating a capture mechanism, routing architecture, or commune layer in operation.

title: Portland’s Socialists Have Built a Political Machine
summary: While New York City gets much of the media attention, the Democratic Socialists of America chapter in Portland, Oregon, has quietly built a local political powerhouse over the last few years.
reason: A socialist organization building durable local electoral infrastructure is a concrete example of routing-level change — moving resources and political power through non-market, non-party circuits.
angle: Use the routing architecture tool to ask what DSA Portland actually routes — money, candidates, voter contact, mutual aid — versus what it represents, and whether that infrastructure is structurally harder to capture than a campaign brand.

title: Xi Jinping’s Chinese Dream Has Replaced the Maoist Credo
summary: China’s leaders now appeal to the vision of a rejuvenated future rather than a revolutionary past. The new social contract between the people and the party state is a pragmatic one: social stability in return for continued economic growth.
reason: This is primarily a representational analysis of ideological branding shift — new messaging replacing old messaging — without illuminating routing-level changes in how power, resources, or care actually flow.

title: The Bases of US Empire Are Crumbling
summary: In recent decades, the basis of US hegemony has shifted from domestic industrial strength to its ability to enforce the rules that organize global production, finance, and money. Today this imperial role is now increasingly under strain.

title: The Volkswagen Crisis Exposes Germany’s Industrial Decline
summary: A proud symbol of German industry, Volkswagen enjoys far-reaching government support. Yet as it leans on the Chinese market, it’s far from clear that the firm is going to save jobs at its German sites.
reason: The VW crisis reveals how state-supported capital uses nationalist alibi (protecting German jobs/industry) while actually routing value extraction through global markets, with workers bearing the cost of that contradiction.
angle: Alibi structure: the 'national champion' narrative that justified decades of state support becomes visible as cover for a firm whose actual productive routing has nothing to do with German workers' welfare.

title: Tech Unionism Against Doomerism
summary: Workers who are developing AI are uniting with those who are under threat from it to enforce regulation and public control.
reason: This describes a concrete routing-level change — workers building cross-sectoral organizational forms that bypass both employer capture and doomerist paralysis — rather than just new messaging about AI risk.
angle: Use the routing architecture tool to show how this coalition routes solidarity across the developer/displaced divide, structurally bypassing the alibi that AI governance must be left to technical experts or regulators.

title: How to Fight a Freeway 101
summary: A new guide gives advocates the basics to building a campaign against harmful infrastructure in their neighborhoods — and the best time to start is now.
reason: A practical guide to resisting infrastructure enclosure directly addresses routing architecture and prefigurative organizing at the neighborhood level.
angle: Frame the guide as a routing-architecture intervention — freeway fights are not just about content (opposing a road) but about which communities get cut off from flows of resources, mobility, and care, and who gets to redesign those circuits.
